scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for the older brother to let his 7-year-old brother stay up late watching a movie with his friend. The older brother, who's 18, was in charge because their mom wasn't home until 1 AM. He made sure his brother went to bed on time, but then his friend came over, and they were being loud, which woke up the little brother. The little brother wanted to stay up and watch the movie, and the older brother initially said no but then let him stay because his friend encouraged it. In the end, the little brother fell asleep on the couch, and the older brother carried him upstairs to bed around midnight. The next morning, the little brother was cranky and didn't want to get up, even though it was the weekend. The mom found out and got mad at the older brother, who thinks that the little brother should understand consequences and that missing two hours of sleep isn't a big deal. So, is the older brother AITA (Ask if it's a Thing) for not making his little brother go to bed? I need to figure out if it's right or wrong and why. First, I think about the little brother's age. He's 7, which is pretty young. Kids at that age need a lot of sleep, and missing out on sleep can really affect their mood and behavior the next day. The older brother knows this because he mentioned that if his brother doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts. So, he's aware of the consequences. On the other hand, the older brother was in a situation where his friend was over, and they were having fun. The little brother was already awake and wanted to join in. The older brother didn't want to deal with the hassle of dragging his brother upstairs and having him throw a fit, especially since his friend was there. He probably didn't want to ruin the fun or make a scene in front of his friend. I also think about the concept of teaching consequences. The older brother believes that the little brother should understand that staying up late leads to feeling bad the next day. However, at 7 years old, it's unclear if the little brother fully grasps that connection. It might be more about the older brother wanting to teach responsibility rather than the little brother being capable of understanding the long-term effects of sleep deprivation. Another angle is the role of the older brother. He's 18, so he's almost an adult, and his mom trusts him enough to leave him in charge. He made sure his brother went to bed on time initially, which shows responsibility. But when the little brother woke up and wanted to stay up, the older brother had to make a decision. He chose to let his brother stay up, which led to the little brother being cranky the next day. I also consider the mom's reaction. She got mad at the older brother for letting his brother stay up late. She probably values the importance of sleep for her young son and was upset that the older brother didn't enforce the bedtime rule, even though he had a valid reason for not wanting to deal with a tantrum in front of his friend. So, is it right or wrong? On one hand, the older brother was trying to maintain a good time with his friend and avoid a confrontation. On the other hand, he knew that his brother needed sleep and that staying up late would have negative consequences. He also thought that missing two hours of sleep wasn't a big deal, but for a 7-year-old, that might be significant. I think it's a bit of both. The older brother showed responsibility by initially putting his brother to bed, but he also made a decision that went against his own knowledge of the importance of sleep. It's understandable that he didn't want to deal with a tantrum, especially with a friend over, but it might have been better to set a boundary and explain to his brother why he needed to go to bed, even if it meant some short-term discomfort. In the end, the older brother might have been AITA because he prioritized avoiding a confrontation over ensuring his brother got enough sleep, which is crucial for his well-being. However, it's also understandable that he wanted to have a good time with his friend without the stress of dealing with a cranky little brother.
